links.outcome: LLM accuracy on structured EHR tasks as table size increased
links.effect: CoT accuracy degraded significantly as table size increased; direct prompting uniformly low; smaller and distilled models had more formatting and execution errors.
links.quote: CoT prompting moderately improved performance, particularly for logical filtering, but results degraded significantly as table size increased.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-generated and executed Python code (tool use) instead of direct or chain-of-thought prompting for structured EHR tabular queries

screen.practice: tool-enabled code generation vs direct/CoT prompting
screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks LLMs on structured EHR administrative tasks, comparing different deployment/prompting practices (direct prompting vs. chain-of-thought vs. tool-augmented code execution) to improve accuracy and guard against errors.

primary.practice: tool-enabled code generation and chain-of-thought prompting
